subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should this request be closed into the canonical workspace-management design, narrowed to a Control UI read-only/workspace-only slice, or approved to include editable/system filesystem scope?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but workspace-wide edits and any system filesystem browser cross Gateway/UI authorization, path-containment, destructive-operation, and sensitive-file boundaries that automation cannot decide.

options.title: Fold Into Canonical Workspace API
options.body: Treat all-workspace editing as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368 and keep system filesystem access out unless maintainers open a separate approved design.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Control UI Slice
options.body: Build a Control UI workspace-only browser/editor on the existing read-only namespace plus a separately approved admin mutation contract, without system scope.

options.title: Approve Full Scope Levels
options.body: Sponsor the three-level selector including system browsing, with explicit auth, read/write policy, auditing, and recovery requirements before implementation.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Canonical Workspace API
recommendation.body: Treat all-workspace editing as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368 and keep system filesystem access out unless maintainers open a separate approved design.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the related read-only workspace browser split and can decide whether this broader Control UI/system-scope request should be narrowed or folded into the canonical design.
